notes.title: OFFLINE VERSION FOR BLITZKRIEG 3
notes.notes:
Officers! IMPORTANT ANNOUNCEMENT!

Blitzkrieg 3 is going offline! We present you the new offline Blitzkrieg 3 build, which will let you enjoy tactical battles of this WWII strategy without having to be connected to the internet. The offline version has all the features, content, and your saved progress from the online version – except, of course, the PvP online mode. However, should you choose to compete, Boris will still be happy to assist you in a friendly duel, opposing his AI skills against yours. 

After you download the latest update, you will have two options at the start of the game – to play the original Blitzkrieg 3 or to play the offline version. Please be aware, that in order to transfer your current progress to the offline version, you have to upload the patch and to run this mode, while the online Blitzkrieg 3 is still available. The servers for Blitzkrieg 3 are planned to be shut down in the recent future, so please don’t put it off. The exact date of shutting the online Blitzkrieg 3 will be announced additionally. 

We hope that you enjoy playing Blitzkrieg 3 offline and wish you splendid victories!

notes.title: Changes in the Demo!
notes.notes:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/3997d6a7f6b0ce2d45ca56cf20db7626c679b54b.jpg[/img]

[h1]What’s new:[/h1]

[b]1) Campaign missions are now available in the Demo![/b]
Before this patch you’ve been busy rising in rating. This allowed you to fight on other eras and expand your army. 
Now, rating is opening campaign missions too! 
This means that you will also be able to try a bit more of a PvE-part of the game before purchase :)

To unlock a mission, you need to receive a certain amount of rating points for fighting in Skirmish. This number corresponds to one of the 7 ranks in the game.
If your rating points number drops down, the mission will become unavailable again (even if you managed to play it before). 

Please remember that additional missions will remain inaccessible in the Demo. 

[b]2) Changes in the rating system[/b]
The amount of rating points received for victories and defeats has been increased threefold. This will allow Demo version players reach 2nd and 3rd eras faster and fight on them.

[h1]Fixed issues:[/h1]

1) Fixed a bug in Sevastopol mission which led to a freeze after certain actions and made the completion of the mission impossible;
2) Fixed a bug in March on Berlin due to which a defeat screen was shown after the final cutscene instead of a victory one;
3) Fixed several historical inaccuracies in Rebellion in Warsaw;
4) Corrected a few mistakes in English and German localizations.

notes.notes:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/c0bf062f230b76fda062e9b400bdd410d2ae6680.jpg[/img]

[h1]What's new:[/h1]

[b]1) Rewind feature in missions[/b]
There were many comments left by Blitzkrieg 3 community members asking for an ability to speed up the units movement around the map. Your wish came true with this patch :)
Now you will be able to play on x2 speed. 
The rewind buttons can be found at the same place they are in Battle Replays:

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/5c1fad371e5256daa32dbba36785583db795d405.jpg[/img]

[b]2) New PvP map[/b]
The new map is called "Mountain waterfall". Its main feature is two absolutely different neighboring climate zones. One side of the map is covered with snow, and the other one has already entered springtime. 
You can read more about it in our previous [url=http://steamcommunity.com/games/235380/announcements/detail/1438193798259958962]Development blog[/url].

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/c92f22453f71d5191290b88cb49a5d544aecd2a1.jpg[/img]

[b]3) 7 new achievements added[/b]
All of the new achievements can be unlocked through completing the first missions of the game. Please note, that those of you, who have already completed them will have to replay them in order to receive new achievements.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/1fe9acd9161597f801e609980887bb88e08dda23.jpg[/img]

4) Reworked tutorial
All the tutorial texts have been rewritten in order to make the game more friendly and understandable for new users. Game tips are shown right over the reserve panel.

5) Added access to Demo through Launcher
Now everyone who is not using Steam to play will be able to play in the Demo too. 
What is more, Launcher users will soon become able to upgrade their Standard editions to Deluxe ones in Launcher. 

[h1]Fixes:[/h1]

1) Some of the reasons disconnects happened were eliminated.
2) Matchmaking search time had been improved. 
3) Some of the authorization issues were fixed.

notes.title: Technical patch №9
notes.notes:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/4596683/54d301d2fa17c6a96d4114a5403971c460446dc5.jpg[/img]

[h1]What’s new:[/h1]
1. We are introducing [b]rank system[/b] into the game!
Ranks demonstrate your battle efficiency. You can level it up both in PvE and PvP. The higher your rank is, the more modern units you will receive for the wins. 
This way, as soon as you unlock the Frontline and win a certain amount of times, you will be able to collect the whole unit park of the game and fight on other eras without completing the missions at all!
Receiving new ranks will also provide you an ability to purchase upgrades for your units (all eras upgrades included) in the Research tab whatever your campaign progression is. 

[h1]Changes:[/h1]
1. Now if you click on your nickname while being on the globe you will be able to see a Player Information screen.
There you can find your current rank, see the next one and learn what you must do to achieve it. Also, Leaderboard had been transferred to this screen.
Through pulling your cursor over the next rank you will be able to see which units will be available for dropping down as rewards after you receive it through fighting in PvP or completing a certain mission. 
2. Enhanced the sorting system of the reserves on the globe.

[h1]Fixed issues:[/h1]
1. Fixed a bug which caused units to behave incorrectly – some of them did not turn to the target, some didn’t shoot.
2. Aviation you called in is no longer is in flames from the start :)
3. Changed Pz II Luhs gun characteristics slightly.

notes.title: Update 0.9.10
notes.notes:
[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/News%202017/Lines2104/GIF1.gif[/img]

Good evening, officers!

A lot of interesting things await you in the [b]0.9.10 [/b]update. Most of the things we’ve added to the game this time were requested by our community. In this post, we’ll briefly tell you about the latest game changes. Click on a specific topic to learn more. Here we go!

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/News%202017/Lines2104/EN_1.png[/img]
You’ve been asking for them. You’ve been waiting for them. And they’re finally here! Based on the numerous requests of fans of the previous parts of the game, as well as fans of military strategies in general, we’ve introduced the ability to move the artillery. You will now be able to control mobile howitzers, anti-tank guns and AA guns. They are available in the game as separate units. You can add them to your assault group or use them as reinforcements. 
If the crew using the fortification is killed, it can be occupied by either your forces or the enemy. 
Mobile artillery can be entrenched. In this position, it loses the ability to move in exchange for increased defense of the gun and the crew. Bear in mind that the entrenched artillery has a limited barrel rotation range, so use this ability wisely to defeat the enemy.
Mobile artillery has low maneuverability, but, similar to infantry, units of this type are disguised when they enter forested areas.

Animation of shooting in many mobile fortifications is not in the final quality.

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/News%202017/Lines2104/EN_2.png[/img]
The next important innovation is a Workshop for units. You’ll be able to improve your tanks, infantry, weapons and even air support using the latest engineering developments. 

Upgrades can be unlocked using research points. You receive research points for battles - the longer you fight and the more efficient you are, the more points you’ll get. 

You need to complete [b]missions[/b] in order to receive research points for them. The command will reward you with engineering resources for successful operations. Note that research points are awarded only [b]one time[/b]!

You receive points differently in [b]PvP[/b] mode. Points are awarded depending on the damage ratio and time spent in battle. Thus, you may receive almost nothing if your opponent is disconnected from the game or if you don’t perform any actions. Be more active! :)

Note that you [b]will not receive research points[/b] for battles arranged through the lobby, including battles against our AI, Boris. 
 
[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/News%202017/Lines2104/EN_3.png[/img]
Many of you who have already advanced to the second and third eras want to fight in the eras you have already completed. You will now have this opportunity! 

Previously, when you entered a new era your base moved with you and you couldn’t return to the previous era. You will now have a base at each phase of the war. You’ll be able to switch between them by changing the era. Each base will need to be equipped and defended, as the success of its defense will affect your rating. Your forces will be restricted to the era you are in and, as a consequence, you will not be able to assign a unit from the third era to protect a base from the second. 

And so, you will be able to play in Assault and Skirmish modes in any of your available eras. 

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/News%202017/Lines2104/EN_4.png[/img]
[h1][b]March on Berlin[/b][/h1]
[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/News%202017/Lines2104/Berlin.png[/img]
The mission takes place in April 1945. Soviet troops are approaching Berlin from the east, encircling the city. According to intelligence reports, to the west of Berlin a large grouping of troops is trying to break free of the encirclement.

Your mission is to locate and attack the group of German troops ready to break through to the west, where, according to intelligence, there are Nazi criminals. You need to provoke them into attack, keep them busy, and hold the western area until the allied forces close the encirclement from the north and south.

[h1][b]V-2[/b][/h1]
While working on the game, we came to the decision that Deluxe edition owners should have an additional mission for each faction. You have probably already managed to complete one such mission for Germany - Dora. V-2 is a deluxe mission for the USSR.

According to our intelligence, the Germans are testing the latest V-2 rockets at the firing area near Debits. We must capture one of these rockets at any cost!

[h1][b]"Monkey temple" - New Map for Skirmish Mode [/b][/h1]
[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/News%202017/Lines2104/hram1.png[/img]
You will be fighting in the Malaysian jungle in a picturesque locale, where many waterfalls roar. The control points on this map are located in a peaceful village, in rice fields, and near an ancient temple. Combat operations were conducted in this area, and so part of the land has been mercilessly charred. But this doesn’t overshadow the jungle’s natural beauty. A feature of the map’s landscape is the abundance of areas covered by water, where passage through it will take longer than through land.

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/News%202017/Lines2104/EN_5.png[/img]
[h1][b]UI and graphics:[/b][/h1]
1. [b]Globe icons have been changed[/b]
[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/News%202017/Lines2104/metki.png[/img]
As you already know, there are several types of missions in the game. We’ve slightly adjusted the look of icons on the globe, and we hope that you will like these changes.

There are two types of missions in the game.
Large icons indicate missions that unlock access to the next phases of the war. Small icons indicate side missions. The color of the mission reflects its difficulty relative to the forces at your command. The icon disappears once the mission has been completed. The shield icon marks your base, where you have to place your troops to defend against assaults.To head into battle against other players, click on the icon with two crossed guns.
 
2. [b]Interface elements have been redesigned[/b]
Changes apply to:
• mission description window (including text);
• window that shows information about your unit;
• window that opens when you place your cursor on a unit;
• now negative effect timers are displayed above units and on the central panel;
• a reload timer has been added for slow-shooting units. 

3. [b]Some weather effects in the game have been redesigned. [/b]

[h1][b]Missions and maps[/b][/h1]
1. Tutorial has been updated and improved.
2. Side mission maps have been improved as well.
3. Maps that house first-era bases, which you can also see in Assault mode, have been redesigned.
4. The "Swamp" and "Ravine" maps have been moved to other eras:
•	"Swamp" has moved to the first era;
•	"Ravine" has moved to the second era.

[h1][b]Technical details: [/b][/h1]
1. The game now loads much faster. 
2. You can now disable voice notifications in the sound settings.
3. You can now select an era in the lobby. 
If you choose, for example, the second era, you can use units only from the first and second eras, etc.
4. We’ve solved problems with the launch of some missions in the Mac version of the game. 

[h1] [b]Known problems:[/b][/h1]
 1. Some images added in this update will be changed or improved.

[h1]For the Axis: Commander of Artillery [b]Georg von Küchler[/b]![/h1]

Georg von Küchler was one of the authors of the German doctrine of combined arms reconnaissance. He participated in World War I, where he received many orders and medals for his actions. In 1919, he volunteered to go to Poland to fight the Red Army. During World War II, he took part in the invasions of Poland, the Netherlands, and Belgium. In 1944, he was forced to resign, but when he was offered a chance to join the plot to assassinate Adolf Hitler known as the 20 July Plot, he refused it. Coming from a family of German officers, he was a real patriot of his Fatherland and believed in its ideals. Küchler learned all of the advantages of conducting reconnaissance in force when he was in Poland. For this purpose, he uses snipers, light vehicles, and anti-tank artillery supported by infantry and assault infantry. His views on defensive warfare were formed under the influence of constant redeployments from one front to another. That's why he prefers light and mobile squads with anti-tank rifles, mortars, and anti-tank guns rather than permanent fortifications.

He was one of the most respected commanders in the British Army. In 1941 he was appointer Commander-in-Chief in India, then he was sent to North Africa to replace Field Marshal A. Wavell as Commander-in-Chief, British Middle East Command. He started preparing an advance operation against German and Italian troops under the command of General Rommel (Operation Crusader). Despite heavy casualties, Auchinleck managed to have some success (breaking the siege of Tobruk). After that, however, Rommel counter-attacked, captured Benghazi on 29th January 1942, and pushed the British forces back to Gazala and Bir Hakeim. Auchinleck moved his reserves up and launched a new attack, defeating Rommel in July 1942 in the Battle of El Alamein.

[i]Premium Units for reaching new levels:[/i]
1) Assault Infantry + Panhard 178;
2) 2 rare Anti-Tank Infantry squads;
3) Machine Gunners and Greyhound!

- Characteristics have become more authentic;
- Now units of different eras are closer in strength; 
Previously units of an older era used to be much stronger than those of the previous one. We have balanced these limits, and now it's the unit's historical characteristics that affect its strength, not a link to a particular period of the war; 
- We have corrected armor characteristics: thanks to your help we found some inconsistencies in our characteristics and corrected them!

[*] [h1] [b]Assault mode has undergone significant changes![/b][/h1]

[h1]Gameplay Changes:[/h1]		[olist]	
[*]All infantry units except snipers are now able to dig trenches. Taking damage or receiving different orders interrupts the digging process.
[*]All armoured vehicles now have the Dig In ability. A unit cannot attack while digging in. Taking damage does not interrupt the process.		
[*]A new mission from the Soviet campaign, The Luga Line, has been added to the game.

[img]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/DEVBLOGS/26/prew_luga_3.png[/img]

[i]In the early stages of the war, the Soviet army was not faring well. Advancing on the German left flank, Army Group North routed the North-Western Front and was already closely approaching Leningrad by the third week of the war. At that point, however, they were stopped at the newly created Luga defensive line. The Germans were stuck there for a month and a half. They were never able to breach the line and eventually flanked it.
You will be tasked with conducting a special operation in the rear to destroy the anti-aircraft cover and hold back the enemy's counteroffensive until reinforcements arrive.[/i]

[*]The commander system has been reintroduced to the game. A number of changes have been made to it. A commander can strengthen some of your troops. Rewards can be earned by raising each commander's loyalty level.
[*]Leaderboards have been reintroduced to the game. These are available through the menu, or by clicking Rankings in the upper left corner.
[*]The reward system for side missions has been changed; you will now receive the units listed in the mission description upon first completion. 	
[*]The provisional shop has been removed from the game. Players who haven't made any purchases in it will get a minimum set of essential units.
[*]The combat and base interfaces have gotten a significant visual overhaul.
[*]The globe's appearance has been changed, and new icons added.	
[*]Owners of the Deluxe and Strategic editions of the game have gotten their statues back.
[*]The March on Daugavpils mission has been significantly simplified.	[/olist]	
		
[h1]Fixed Issues:	[/h1]	[olist]		
[*]Fixed the freezes that previously affected all side missions, most notably the Essential Provisions side mission.			
[*]Turning on vertical sync no longer causes a frame rate drop.
[*]Fixed freezes occurring when the opponent calls in new troops.	
[*]Removed a delay in the interface response to pressing buttons.
[*]Fixed a bug causing players to stop receiving support points mid-combat during a skirmish.	
[*]Corrected historical inaccuracies on some of the commander portraits.
[*]Fixed a bug in the Large Calibre side-mission whereby completing the task to eliminate gun crews would fail to register.	
[*]Fixed a bug in the March on Daugavpils mission whereby reinforcements could not be requested despite available reserve troops and sufficient support points.	
[*]Added missing unit tooltips in the pre-battle window.			[/olist]

[h1]Known Issues:	[/h1]		[olist=1]	
[*]Functionality for assessing a commander's bonuses is yet to be implemented.	
[*]Incorrect shell explosion effects above trenches.
[*]Mouse-wheel scrolling does not work when viewing statistics and in matches’ results.
[*]Puddles may incorrectly display on top of trenches.	
[*]A white square will appear instead of the image in the pop-out message if you click on missions that are not implemented in the game yet. 
[*]Menu will not pop out after you cancel PvP search (it will show up after you open any mission up). 
[*]Pillboxes’ timers work incorrectly.
[*]Slots for infantry in fortifications are not always shown.
[*]The progress of assaulting houses is not shown.
[*]If you own a low-spec PC, you may face some issues with FPS in Luga (first Soviet mission).

notes.notes:
[img]http://s019.radikal.ru/i615/1608/b8/18a0ae588ef3.gif[/img]

Commanders, we would like to invite you to try this wide-ranging update full of exciting changes: a campaign on behalf of the Axis countries, a modified economy, a rarity system, and a temporary store.

The General Staff urges you to promptly report all errors and inaccuracies you encounter in combat. Contribute to the project’s development and help it improve even more!

[h1]What’s new?[/h1]
[list][*][b]A full-blown German campaign has been added.[/b]
You will have 7 missions that cover the main periods of the war and show the role of special forces in significant operations. We’ve done our best to make them as historically accurate as possible.

[*][b]Two new missions have been added to the campaign: [/b]
The Battle of El Alamein and the Siege of Sevastopol.

[i]The Battle of El Alamein:[/i]
The Panzer Army Africa under Rommel’s command has suffered a defeat against the British, who used their greatly superior forces and air supremacy to break through the German frontlines and start pursuing the enemy troops. The Italian forces that Rommel left without vehicles have been taken prisoner.
The taskforce must attack a British base far behind enemy lines. The goal of the attack is to distract the enemy and deprive it of the supplies it needs for an offensive. The taskforce can count on any assistance from the remaining German forces.

[i]The Siege of Sevastopol:[/i]
The 11th Army under Manstein’s command has received an order to take Sevastopol at any cost. A significant number of Luftwaffe forces and unlimited ammo have been supplied to complete the objective.
Supported by heavy vehicles, your taskforce has to break through to the shore of Severnaya Bay and ensure fire adjustment for the siege artillery on the mooring areas to prevent the Soviet command from transferring ammunition and reinforcements to Sevastopol.

[*][b]9 secondary missions have been added.[/b]
In addition to key campaign missions, some extra PvE battles will be available. You will receive rewards for your victories and be able to toughen up your troops and commanders in combat and increase their stats.

[*][b]The game’s economic system has been changed.[/b]
You can no longer purchase units for resources (except for the temporary store). You will receive rewards for participating in battles. You will be able to gain access to new vehicles, infantry, weapons, and obstructions during combat. Exactly what depends on the game mode and map.

[*][b]Tiers have been removed from the game.[/b]

[*][b]All player rankings will be reset [/b]and divided for different modes. No leaderboard is available in the current version, but this is temporary.

[*]You will not lose your previous progress: you will immediately go to the corresponding war period (starting from this version it will divided into 3 eras). However, you will lose all vehicles, infantry, and obstructions and have to assemble your army again. [b]For a limited time only, a store been added to the game[/b] where you can buy various units for a temporary currency. You will get a certain number of glory points depending on your progress, tier, and rank in the record table.

[*][b]The main menu has been removed from the game.[/b]

[*]New players now choose a faction immediately and start the game with the Poland mission. When they log in next time, they are immediately transferred to the [b]global map[/b]. This window will show all available battles, transfers to the base and between eras, a player’s army, the system menu, news, etc. All stores have been removed from your combat section. A parade ground where your vehicles will be shown has been added. The appearance of the base will reflect your progress and correspond to the historical era.

[*]Now, before entering any battle (including a single-user PvE),[b] a player assembles a detachment from the vehicles and infantry at their disposal.[/b] Units taken into combat must suit the conditions of the historical operation (in terms of years and purpose). Part of the detachment can be available when the battle starts, while the remainder can be available later, for use as reinforcements.

[*][b]Many changes have been made in the balance for the Skirmish and Assault modes, including [/b] alterations to attack limits and generating Reinforcement Points and Victory Points. General combat stats for vehicles have also been recalculated, including side/rear damage, aiming time, accuracy at close range etc.

[*][b]The total number of units has almost doubled.[/b]

[*]The commander system and chat will be [i]temporarily[/i] unavailable. Also, since the trench system is being reworked, there are no trenches at bases for now.

[*][b]To change faction[/b] in this version of the game, you need to go to your base. While being on it, press ESC and choose the necessary option in the menu.

[*]If you are tier 1 or 2, you will have to replay the first mission of the game. If you reached higher tiers, “Capture of Poland” will be completed with 1 star automatically. You will receive a reward for 1 star walkthrough, also.
[/list]

notes.title: Update 0.8.5
notes.notes:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/UPDATES/085ENG.jpg[/IMG]

[h1]What's New?[/h1]
[list]
[*]We've added Skirmish! Your goal in this mode is to increase your score by capturing and holding control points. At the moment there is only one symmetrical map available, but we plan to add more. This map includes three control points and a number of fortified strategic points. Right now, it's very important for us to thoroughly test the playability of this game mode and the map. For example: for the final version of the map, we want to create the feeling that the German line of defense was recently here and that now a head-on battle for this line is taking place. You can learn more about Skirmish mode, and how it differs from Assault mode, in [url=http://steamcommunity.com/games/235380/announcements/detail/604985283924292620]developer diaries #12[/url].
[*]This new mode also presents previously unavailable fortifications, such as damaged tank pillboxes that cannot be assaulted, only destroyed. These can be a big help in defending captured points, but to use them, the player first needs to repair them.
[*]Skirmish includes 1v1, 2v2, and 3v3 battles. However, the matchmaking lobby is currently unavailable. We're planning to add it in the next update.
[*]Pathfinding has been completely reworked. Vehicles don't get "stuck" anymore and are better at reacting to orders and plotting courses. We mentioned this in [url=http://steamcommunity.com/games/235380/announcements/detail/598230758564383462]developer diaries #13[/url].
[*]We've added bump mapping for terrain textures.
[*]Unit attack priorities have been adjusted. 
[*]Once you have seen fortifications in the fog of war, you'll only see the status they had when you last saw them. You can also command a unit to attack them.
[*]The in-game options menu allows you to choose from several variants of how units are grouped in the reinforcements panel.
[*]Whenever you hover over any friendly, enemy, or neutral object during combat, you'll see a tooltip (a pop-up window) with information about the object's name, class, durability, and current HP.
[*]Fortifications are now more durable. They don't stop working after the first encounter, they can be recaptured several times without being destroyed, and they protect their positions throughout the whole game.
 [/list]

After a few days (on June 10), once we have a good idea of your impressions and an idea of the big picture, we'll arrange an in-game poll about this update. Don't forget to participate!

notes.title: Hotfix
notes.notes:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/news2016/0802bUSA.jpg[/IMG]

A small update has been deployed, which has fixed an issue with the Assault mode winning conditions. In some cases, the winner was wrongly designated, receiving ressources and rating without meeting the winning criteria.

[b]The winning conditions for both sides are now as follows:[/b][list]
[*]Destroy opponents Headquarters
[*]Destroy opponents Communication Centre and all units
[*]Opponent leaves the game
[/list]
[b]How is it determined, if a victory is minor or major (attacker)?[/b][list]
[*]Triumph - the attacker wins (according to the above mentioned conditions), managing to capture at least one control point.
[*]Victory - the attacker wins without capturing any control points
[*]Defeat - the attacker loses, with at least one control point captured
[*]Crushing Defeat- the attacker loses without capturing any control points at all.
[/list]
For the defending player, the victory conditions are a mirror reflection of the above-mentioned list.

[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/news2016/STEAM08_hotfixes_EN.jpg[/IMG]

After reviewing your feedback, we have decided to increase the significance of pre-planned defense in relation to direct combat defense. To achieve this, we have increased the limit of the troops and fortifications for the defender, and at the same time reduced the impact of reinforcement points flow from CP.

[B]Set the following limits:[/B]
[LIST]
[*]Assaulter set limit: 250/300/400/525/650/775/900
[*]Defender set limit: 150/225/300/350/400/450/500
[*]Fortifications limit: 130/130/190/250/305/380/475
[*]Maximum limit of  the army in the battle: 450/525/650/775/900/1050/1200
[/LIST]

[B]Parameters of the reinforcement points were modified:[/B]
[LIST]
[*]The basic generation was reduced to 3 points per 5 seconds.
[*]Generation for the owning a CP (control points) was reduced to 1,5/2,25/3 for 1/2/3 CP.
[*]A multiplier was moved to after ⅙ of standard combat timer, gradually increasing the reinforcement point generation until a maximum at ½ of the combat session timer
[*]The maximum of this multiplier was increased to 3.5.
[/LIST]

[B]Other balancing changes:[/B]

notes.notes:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/news2016/08steamEN.jpg[/IMG]

In anticipation of the celebration of the end of the War in the European Theatre, we would like to invite you, commanders, to try this big new update full of exciting changes. 

[h1]What’s new?[/h1]
[list]
[*]Three new missions for the German campaign: North Africa, Daugavpils Rush, and Arras.
[*]Completely redesigned Assault mode:
1)	The player’s main objective (victory condition) is to destroy the enemy’s headquarters, instead of the earlier requirement to capture the Control Points within a particular period of time;
2)	Control Points are now points of interest for the player, not the final objective. Their role is secondary: they increase Reinforcement Point generation;
3)	A new reinforcement summoning system has been introduced: the player uses Reinforcement Points to request troops from the base that haven’t been used as advance forces (all the troops available at the base are available in battle).
4)	Reinforcement Points are continually earned during the battle, as well as when a Control Point is successfully captured. The amount of points credited depends on the number of Control Points under the player’s control: each subsequent CP captured will grant fewer points. For instance, when you capture your first control point (or re-capture it after losing all of your control points), you score more points for it than for the last control point.
5)	Opponents have varying cooldown (recharge time) and point limits. The attacker has many more troops at the beginning of the battle, but the defender has three Control Points and a quicker Reinforcement Point generation rate. 
6)	This approach allows for a “see-saw” system, making it easy to get back into the battle. Example: the attacker has thrown all his troops into the battle and almost made it to the HQ. Meanwhile the defender managed to save up enough points and summoned troops that effectively resisted the attacking force. Once the attacker has been driven back to his starting position, he can summon forces optimally suited to fight the defender’s current forces. Thus players will be able to steal the initiative from each other. 
7)	The attacker now has a reinforcement point for his attack, a base of sorts. The defender’s base has also been redesigned. Destroying the enemy’s HQ now automatically scores a victory, while destroying their Communication Centre deprives them of reinforcements and supports.
[*]The central panel has been redesigned for battle. A reinforcement panel has been added, and the support panel has been redesigned. However, the interface is still not informative enough, and a number of our solutions are temporary. We are working hard on it and will soon improve the situation. 
[*]New thematic loading screens have been added.
[*]The launcher has been removed for all Steam players. News and maintenance announcements are now shown in the main menu, and updating is conducted via Steam servers.
[*]Numerous balance adjustments: unit speed, support cooldown time, ranged effects. We are still working on this and will continue doing so far into the future. So we’d greatly value your comments about the balance of our redesigned Assault mode.
[*]Players can place more infantry squads in some houses than in others, depending on their size.
[*]New support added: Fighter. Smoke Screen and Paratroopers supports have been reworked. Paratroopers now land from aircraft which can be shot down.
[*]The defending AI now uses supports and reacts to the player’s actions more aggressively and actively. But we are still working on this, and significant improvements will be ready by May or June.
[*]Steam authorisation has been significantly sped up; the Leaderboard now loads much more quickly.
[/list]

[h1]Fixed Issues[/h1]
[list]
[*]Improved game stability (frequent crashes were reported after the January 27th patch).
[*]Several squads can now be treated at the same time on the first mission of the Single Player campaign (Poland).
[*]The crashes during the town capture in the first mission of the Single Player campaign (Poland) have been fixed.
[*]An issue causing incomplete update installation when there is insufficient hard disk space (freezing during the game logo) has been fixed.
[*]Flags used during battle have been replaced with correct ones (the attacker’s flags were previously shown on the defender’s Control Points).
[*]Paratroopers no longer “jump” on the roofs of buildings while walking.
[*]The incorrect behaviour of the patrolmen in the first mission of the Single Player campaign (Poland) has been fixed: when troops were trying to circle around a patrol, and at the start of battle, the patrolmen continued walking along their routes as if nothing had happened.
[*]We’ve fixed an incorrect behaviour of infantry during an abrupt change in movement direction: an infantry squad, when ordered to run in the opposite direction, used to first turn towards where ordered but then resume moving in its initial direction.
[/list]

[h1]Known problems to be fixed later:[/h1]
[list]
[*]Attack Aircraft attacks base buildings instead of units
[*]Incorrect location of icons on the minimap
[*]Reinforcements available to call after the battle is over
[*]Upgrading a fortification cancels the selection
[*]When leaving trenches, infantry doesn’t follow orders
[*]Severe game freezing when capturing a building with obstructions using several infantry squads
[*]No visual effects for AT landmine explosions
[*]Incorrect animation of snipers when shooting
[*]Units stand above a trench while sitting in it
[*]Cutscenes in the Daugavpils mission may work incorrectly (lag) on some PC configurations 
[*]Objects on the minimap may be displayed incorrectly (with their positions shifted)
[/list]

notes.title: Update 0.7.2
notes.notes:
[IMG]http://images.akamai.steamusercontent.com/ugc/312244513767631974/00B03FB73BD4DD5289328AE296930AE22FE3AD7E/[/IMG]

Good afternoon, commander!

By popular demand of the commissioned officers of the battlefronts and armies, the Blitzkrieg 3 Experimental Establishment has thoroughly inspected the current combat system to implement a higher level of realism.
[list]
[*]In earlier versions of the game, battles were not always like real life. Soldiers could be injured by a dozen rifle bullets and still be alive. Now most combat units are destroyed with a few hits, but the chances a unit will miss have been increased to compensate. 
[*]New random weather effects have been added to the Multiplayer Campaign: rain and fog. Each of these significantly affects combat tactics.
[*]Moving targets are harder to hit, but firing while moving is harder, too.
[*]Now all infantry units are capable of capturing buildings, but Assault Infantry remain the most effective.
[*]Mines have become invisible. Regular Infantry can use their Clear Minefield ability without restraints.
[*]Bunkers can be stormed and re-captured.
[*]Unit visibility ranges have been changed. To deliver fire effectively across long distances, Tanks and Tank destroyers need infantry support.
[*]Tactical support actions have been completely rebalanced, with all unrealistic types being removed.
[*]Some types of Tank Destroyers now have an indirect fire option, just like their real-world counterparts.
[*]The player now must press any key to start the battle once the map/mission is completely loaded.
[*]Improved leaderboards UI.
[*]Single-player missions have been reworked to adjust to the new balance.
[/list]
Nival Headquarters hopes that battlefront and army commanders will like these changes and calls for detailed feedback in the comments section.

notes.title: Update 0.6.10
notes.notes:
[h1]What's New[/h1]

[b]1)[/b]Since some players who didn't want to lose their defence rating switched to twinks when they were absent, we have added a 48-hour cooldown between base changes. After moving to a different base, players will only be able to move again after two days.

[b]2)[/b]To encourage better use of MLRS, we have added charges limiting their use per session. There are now only 5 salvos for both attack and defence, which should be enough to receive the necessary fire support without using scorched earth tactics.

[b]3)[/b]The starting time has been increased to 70-75% of the total time pool. Also, you will now get +10%, +15%, or +25% for a captured control point (depending on how many points there are on the map).

[b]4)[/b]Aircraft have been rebalanced once again. Their support point cost has been reduced. Damage dealt to vehicles by assault infantry has been increased.

[b]5)[/b]Many types of support are now more effective:
[list]
[*]Smoke Screen's duration has been increased by 50%
[*]Number of shells have been increased for Howitzer Salvo and Howitzer Fire
[*]Howitzer support cooldown has been increased to 1 second
[*]The cost to Capture Fortification has been reduced to 3 (2 if the Fortification is a Commander's)
[*]The cost of engineer support has been reduced to 1 (but range has been increased by 30%, if the support belongs to a Commander)
[/list]

[b]6)[/b]The cost of howitzers (fortifications) in support points has been increased from 62 to 69.


[b]7)[/b]The number of available obstructions has been reduced by a third.

[b]8)[/b]Combat controls have been updated:
[list]
[*]Right-clicking a unit's icon in the central panel centres the camera on the unit, instead of highlighting all identical units as before. You can still highlight all identical units by right-clicking one of them on the map or by holding Ctrl and left-clicking the unit.
[*]Pressing Shift + a number adds highlighted units to the group assigned to that number. If there is no group assigned to this number, the shortcut works the same as Ctrl+Number.
[/list]

[b]9)[/b]All Generals have been renamed Commanders, which is a more accurate word for the tasks they perform. This does not include texts where "general" is used to describe the Commander's rank.

•	The Blitzkrieg 3 game engine has been transferred to the new version of Unity (Unity 5). This will help us speed up the development process and continue to improve the game. Because of the update, all game content has undergone changes, and this has resulted in a large update.
•	Players can now buy any number of any fortifications and place them at their discretion, limited only by their fortifications Supply Points (dependant on map and player tier).
•	The upgrade system has been redesigned. We have also added the MLRS upgrade, the third upgrade option, and the fifth Gear for all units.
•	The gear system has new stats. For example, the stealth upgrade that decreases the detection range of a unit in forests and tall grass.
•	A new default unit ability, Hold Fire, has been added to the game. If selected, units won’t attack until they are spotted. Without Hold Fire mode, units will attack enemies in range irrespective of their stealth status.
•	Session timer mechanics and the number of Support Points have changed. Now, when a battle begins players get less time and Support Points, but gain more time and Support Points for capturing Control Points.
•	Anti-aircraft guns are now able to attack infantry and vehicles. Aircraft remain high-priority targets.
•	Search limits will now be expanded in matchmaking if no players are found in the specified range of base power/rank.
•	The mechanics of machine gun fire have changed. Now, machine gunners don’t fire all of their bullets in a burst at one infantryman target, but instead spray the area with a certain amount of scatter. Also, when machine guns fire, a suppression effect is applied to the target, forcing enemies to get down and reducing some of their combat stats.
•	The ability to fire at specifically-designated areas has been added for machine gun squads. All infantry in the target area will take damage and have the suppression effect applied to them.
•	All aircraft have been rebalanced to make them stronger.
•	Units, fortifications, and limits have been rebalanced in the first few tiers. Battles are now slower and units harder to kill.
•	The economy in the first few tiers has been recalculated.

•	The upgrade system has been redesigned. We have also added the MLRS upgrade, the third upgrade option, and the fifth Gear for all units.
•	The gear system has new stats. For example, the stealth upgrade that decreases the detection range of a unit in forests and tall grass.
•	A new default unit ability, Hold Fire, has been added to the game. If selected, units won’t attack until they are spotted. Without Hold Fire mode, units will attack enemies in range irrespective of their stealth status.
•	Session timer mechanics and the number of Support Points have changed. Now, when a battle begins players get less time and Support Points, but gain more time and Support Points for capturing Control Points.
•	Anti-aircraft guns are now able to attack infantry and vehicles. Aircraft remain high-priority targets.

notes.notes:
[IMG]http://static.blitzkrieg.com/devblog/devblog41.jpg[/IMG]

[h1]Comrade, you have an MLRS at your command![/h1]

Commander, we are happy to inform you that Multiple Launch Rocket Systems are now at your disposal. You can even give them a try right now on the new Tier 7 PvP King of the Hill map! Besides this, Command HQ needs you to carry out PvE Operation Spreewald – rescue prisoners of war and retrieve top secret documents while you’re at it. To help you achieve these goals, you will have Generals of Artillery and of Sabotage Operations at your disposal. 

Among other things, our experts have been working on training the vehicle crews. They now respond to orders better, and no longer lose speed when moving along complex trajectories. With their new instructions, they’ll no longer be homing in on enemy hedgehogs, barbed wire, statues, and other non-aggressive objects. We have also worked on improving communications between unit commanders: a message history tab has been added to chat (players can now see the last 100 chat messages), as well as a Combat Chat tab in which players can send messages to each other in Active Defence mode.

[url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/235380/discussions/0/618459931321255936/#c523897653303355289]Actual list of bugs on 0.6.7 update[/url]

[LIST]
[*]Now, when a unit is rearmed to a new tier, all of its upgrades remain. Experience obtained by units will still be recalculated.
[*]Unit sorting has been improved in the central panel, both on base and in combat. Units are now arranged as follows: Type -> Tier -> Upgrade Gears -> Unit Level
[*]Shadow borders have been reworked on all maps.
[*]Added USSR Mission #6, Spreewald, to the mission selection interface. In this mission, we liberate camp prisoners and capture documents that are important to High Command.
[*]Added a new Tier 7 map: King of the Hill. All new players who reach a level 7 base will be transferred to this map. When the maps are rebalanced, the chances of moving to this map will be reduced.
[*]A new unit class, Rocket Artillery, is now available on Tier 7: the BM-13 Katyusha for the USSR, the Sherman Calliope for the Allies, and the Panzerwerfer 42 Auf.Sf for Germany. An MLRS can use a rocket salvo to fire at a target from a long distance.
[*]Two new generals are available for each faction: the Artillery General and the Special Ops General, each with his own features.
[*]To improve our pathfinding system, we have optimized the movement of vehicles when turning. Now units respond to orders better and no longer lose speed when moving along a complex trajectory.
[*]Now vehicles ignore enemy hedgehogs, barbed wire, statues, and other non-aggressive objects as targets and do not home onto them.
[*]A message history has been added to chat so that players can now see the last 100 chat messages.

notes.title: DevBlog 3: After Implementing the Update
notes.notes:
[IMG]http://ru.blitzkrieg.com/forum/attachment.php?attachmentid=8580&d=1440786112[/IMG]

[B]New Tooltips[/B]

If you have already had a chance to try Update 0.6.6, you might have noticed that unit tooltips have changed.

This UI component previously showed little information and raised more questions than it gave answers. Our task was to fit a large amount of information into a small window before the new combat system was introduced. We understood how important it was not only to bring you information that would be useful for gameplay (such as “this unit is effective against that unit”) but also to introduce some of the historical education that everyone is expecting from us.
As a result, all information shown in a tooltip has been divided into the following sections:
[LIST]
[*]Unit description (what units are used for, i.e. the key to using them effectively)
[*]Durability (or hit points)
[*]Armour (for vehicles only: front, side, and back armour thickness in mm)
[*]Weapons (two types, as a rule: primary and secondary)
[/LIST]

Players can research unit improvements (Gears) in the Engineering Works. Upgrades are different for vehicles and infantry. For instance, we enhance optics for tanks, but we increase shooting accuracy for infantry. Now, instead of displaying the total effect of all upgrades, we show a simplified version of that information, where strokes represent the number of identical upgrades for each type of unit. This also makes the information easier to process.

Not everything with the new tooltips has been polished yet, and they might contain errors. We’ll be glad if you point them out for us. In the meantime, we are planning a lot of chat improvements that will be implemented step by step. These include: fixing bugs; correcting the colour of messages, nicknames, and tiers; preserving status, position, and active tab in chat when the player leaves it; introducing various minor transparency fixes, highlighting a tab when it receives a new message, and changing the position of chat headlines.

We also are preparing the combat selection UI (battle vs. AI, battle vs. real players, defence test) and thinking about texturing the UI (we’d like to add damage, roughness, and so on. We will probably be making these amendments very soon, but they will hardly be major changes, just cosmetic ones).
...
[B]to be continued soon :)[/B]

[B]Added Cologne, a new historical mission for the Allies. [/B]
The player must clear the city of the German forces still remaining after extended bombardment. The battle is set against the background of the beautiful Cologne Cathedral under continuous missile artillery fire. We have also added English and German voiceovers to some missions.

[B]Generals added. [/B]
All players have now access to a default General, a General of Tanks, a General of Infantry, and a General of Aircraft. Each military leader has excellent skills that improve the stats of both individual units and all detachments under his command. For example, the US Air Force under "Hap" Arnold's command cooperates well with ground forces and can prove its worth in offensive combat, while Montgomery can form ground vehicles and defensive fortifications into a steel first, making your base an impregnable fortress. [B]The balance of all units has been completely revised to reflect historical reality. [/B]

[B]Players now have access to two extra bases belonging to other factions, which they can upgrade in parallel with their main one. [/B]
If you want to go to a different base, select the corresponding item in the Esc menu. When one of the bases is selected, all others become "frozen," i.e. they cannot be attacked or get any resources.

Over the last month, all players were earning their rating. Now this will be the main factor that influences matchmaking. The matchmaking system will also take into account the player's base development level.

[B]Added trenches.[/B]
We have added to the game the option to dig trenches and place an infantry squad inside. When in a trench, infantry take less damage. You can take infantry out of a trench at any moment and send them into combat. Enemy trenches can be taken if you kill the enemies inside them.

[B]Chat changes.[/B]
The chat design has been changed to be less intrusive and more ergonomic.

[B]New living creatures.[/B]
There are new living beings on some maps, including animals enjoying every minute of their existence.

[B]Sniper girls.[/B]
Now all Soviet sniper squads include two beautiful girls ready to destroy enemy personnel at the drop of a hat.

[B]Soldiers with AT rifles.[/B]
Soviet anti-tank infantry now have AT rifles on the first three tiers to fight against armoured vehicles with. On subsequent tiers, they are armed with lend-lease rocket launchers.

[B]UI changes.[/B]
When hovering over or upgrading a unit, real performance characteristics are displayed, along with any changes to in-game stats that are directly related to them.

[B]Fortification management.[/B]
We have added an option to manage your fortifications in Active Defence mode and select targets for them to attack.

[B]Moving backwards.[/B]
The odd game logic where a vehicle seemed to choose on its own which side would face in the proper direction when moving to a specified point has been replaced by manual controls. Now you have a corresponding key (B by default) on the command panel to move backwards. You can also move a tank backwards by holding the CTRL key and right-clicking on the target location. When you send a vehicle the normal way, it will always move forward.

notes.title: Update 0.6.5
notes.notes:
[h1][b]Good Day Comrades![/b][/h1]

[H1]What’s New.[/H1]

•	Tier 7 (this HQ upgrade costs 148500) unlocks three new maps: Dam, Large Coal Quarry, and Hills. Each map has three control points and one base.

•	As we prepare to implement faction differences, we have rebalanced the units, allowing us to make interactions between classes more realistic. You can view the complete list of changes at the [url=http://en.blitzkrieg.com/forum/showthread.php?t=1954]following link[/url].

•	We have added Anzio, a fourth historical mission for the Allies that concentrates on urban combat. 

•	We have added the Construction Crew, a new type of support costing one charge, and allowing you to disarm mines or dismantle Czech hedgehogs.

•	The tutorial is now made up of several steps, and players can choose sections most relevant to them and skip the others.

•	Ratings are now calculated correctly, and a single combined rating is used for defence and attack.

•	If you own the Strategic or Deluxe Edition, you’ll be able to build a monument to one of your faction’s great leaders: Lenin for the USSR, Lincoln for the Allies, and Bismarck for Germany. This costs 500 resources.

•	You can no longer challenge an opponent to battle in chat more than once per minute. The attacker will always receive a message if the opponent declines the battle.

•	The chat nicknames of players who bought the Deluxe Edition are now displayed in silver.

•	The chat nicknames of players who bought the Strategic Edition are now displayed in gold.

•	In the UI, the number of units deployed by the attacker and the defender is now shown instead of displaying the enemy’s stored resources.

•	Now, when searching for opponents using the Assault button, players can’t attack bases in their own factions; however, attacking your own faction is available through chat.

•	If a player hasn’t completed a single mission, they will be invited to play PvE at the base once per day. If they haven’t played PvP, they will be invited just as often to join multiplayer from the mission selection screen.

•	We have improved our pathfinding system, allowing us to fix the issue where infantry got stuck on bridges and in cliffs.

•	If a player is at the base and the game is minimized, they will receive a sound message notifying them that they’re being attacked, and the game icon will flash in the taskbar.

•	If an attempt to attack is made and the opponent has no units deployed for defence, they will be informed of this after agreeing to the session. The player can then either observe the attack (with an empty troop pool) or decline and let the attacker carry out an asynchronous attack.

•	A new tab for future generals has been added to the central panel.

•	The info screen is displayed in the main menu once per day, the first time you log in. 

•	Now you can move faster around the map by holding the middle mouse button in a session or the left mouse button at the base. Movement speed has been doubled.

notes.title: Update 0.6.4 / Обновление 0.6.4
notes.notes:
Good Day Comrades!
After our last update development team has been making great progress.
In cooperation with the Main Command of the Armed Forces we have developed two new PVE scenarios and successfully re-balanced the existing one. We have implemented a radical revision of the existing game balancing along with the economics system and resolved a large number of other issues.

[h1]Here is the full list of changes and improvements[/h1]

[B]What’s new?[/B]
[list]
[*]New historical mission “Operation Niwi”.
[*]New historical mission “Kustrin Fortress”.
[*]Historical mission “Neisse Crossing” has been re-balanced.
[*]Control points acquisition rewards have been redistributed. Each next captured control point provides more resources than the previous one.
[*]New information panel added to the in base-view when no building is selected.
[*]New support type – “Incendiary projectile”.
[*]New support type – “Tank reinforcement”.
[*]New support type – “Infantry reinforcement”.
[*]New faction 3D-scene in main menu added.
[*]New icons for buildings and fortifications.
[/list]

[B]Balance and Economics changes[/B]
[list]
[*]Recourses per hour acquisition rate has been increased.
[*]Buildings prerequisites have been simplified.
[*]From Tier 4 onwards, the amount of support points has been increased. 
[*]Units power growth rate connected with new Tier acquisition has been increased from 1.38 to 1.5.
[*]Some units’ cost has increased.
[*]SU-85 reloading time has decreased from 4.5 to 3.45. The damage has decreased accordingly.
[*]The damage radius of tank machine-guns has decreased from 35 to 30.
[*]The session time across all Tiers has increased by one minute.
[/list]

[B]Resolved issues[/B]
[list]
[*]Fortified tank near the building did not attack the infantry placed on its sides.
[*]The experience amount gained by dealing damage was too low.
[*]GUI did not display resources expenses per battle.
[*]Damage dealt to “Landing troops” was too low.
[*]“End battle” button needed to be clicked twice.
[*]Hill-based fortifications were displayed not as expected.
[*]Anti-tank infantry damage radius was displayed incorrectly.
[*]Dead infantry animations sometimes were displayed incorrectly.   
[*]x3 resources bonus was displayed after non-prize battles.
[*]Bunkers did not attack infantry in buildings.
[/list]

[B]Known issues[/B]
[list]
[*]Bonuses acquired by upgrading units in the Science center are in the re-balancing stage and have some issues with displaying.
[*]Bunched units do not attack the enemy without an order.
[*]Possible game crashes while constantly Alt-Tabbing.
[*]Terrain buff affects infantry in buildings.
[*]Units from the same squad can have different grenade-throw speeds.
[*]Verifying the integrity of game cache leads to downloading 97 game files.
[*]Launcher interface localization is in progress.
[*]Bunkers cannot be mined.
[*]Assault infantry throw anti-tank grenades with a large delay.
[*]Low frame rate with in-game explosion effects.
[*]Assault infantry fires armored vehicles.
[*]Camera map-marker mismatches with real camera position.
[/list]

notes.notes:
This update is designed to fix two major technical issues we have, as well as to bring some game changes and improvements. 

[b]Bugs fixed:[/b]
[list]
[*]The bug with "freezing" the game session at 100% combat loading is fixed. If this problem comes up again - within an hour after its appearance, it will be corrected automatically and will no longer prevent you from playing.
[*]The bug with combining accounts with "incorrect symbols" in the nicknames is fixed. Changing nickname procedure while binding the active Closed Alpha account to Steam is obligatory now.
[*]A number of minor technical bugs fixed.
[/list]

[b]Common:[/b]
Right now we are testing our anti-bot system, so there is a limitation of the amount of battles a day. Yet with this update it has been significantly increased: now you will be getting the resources for the victory in up to 100 attacks a day (instead of 25). 

[b]Support:[/b]
The cost of air support at the 5th level of development significantly decreased: 3 points for reconnaissance aircraft (instead of 5), and 4 points for assault aircrafts (instead of 6).
